What actually moves an app on the Play Store

Nine thousand Android apps, cleaned and cross-referenced with sixty thousand user reviews. Explore the market, then test what a rating model can and can't tell you.

Google Play Store dataset · 10,841 raw rows reduced to unique apps after removing one corrupted record and deduplicating by app name

Landscape

Thirty-three categories, but they are nothing like equal. Two of them hold almost a third of the store, and the crowded ones are not the ones with the happiest users.

Category landscape

Average rating against total installs. Bubble area is the number of apps; colour is the share that charge money. Hover for detail.

How crowded each category is

App count. Click a bar to filter the market map above.

Installs are won by a handful of categories

Total installs, log scale, against the median app in that category — the gap between the two shows how top-heavy a category is.

The biggest apps in the store

The 60 most-installed apps. Sortable by any column.

Ratings

Ratings are not a spread — they are a pile. The store compresses almost everything into the 4.0 to 4.6 range, which makes the small differences that remain worth taking seriously.

Where every rating falls

Count of apps per tenth of a star. Pick a category to overlay it against the whole store.

Rating spread by category

The middle half of each category's apps, with the median marked.

Does app size matter?

Average rating by size band, with app counts behind.

Does staying updated matter?

Average rating by the year an app was last updated.

Who the app is for

Average rating by content rating.

What moves with what

Pearson correlation. Reviews and installs are log-transformed first. Hover a cell for the value.

When apps get updated

Update activity by month and year. The store's visible history is heavily weighted to the months before the snapshot.

Money

Paid apps are a rounding error in volume but not in behaviour. They are rated differently, sized differently, and reach a fraction of the audience.

Free against paid

Share of the store, and how the two groups differ.

What paid apps charge

Price distribution below $30, where almost all paid apps sit.

Reach costs money

Median installs for a free app against a paid one, log scale.

Where the paid money would be

Price multiplied by installs, summed per category. Read this as an upper bound, not a revenue figure — see the note below.

How much of each category charges

Share of apps that are paid, against the category's average rating.

Sentiment

Star ratings compress everything into a narrow band. Review text does not — the same 4.2-star category can hide wildly different levels of user frustration.

How every review reads

Polarity of reviews, from hostile at −1 to delighted at +1. The spike at zero is factual or neutral text.

Sentiment by category

Share of reviews that read positive, neutral and negative. Categories with more than 100 reviews only.

The gap between stars and words

Average star rating against the share of reviews that read positive. Categories below the line are rated more generously than they are talked about.

Predict a rating

A gradient boosting model trained on rated apps, running live in your browser. It uses six features — the ones that survived permutation-importance screening of the original twelve. Dropping price, content rating, minimum Android version and the rest cost almost no accuracy, which tells you how little they mattered. Move any input, or hit Random app to load a real app from the held-out data.

Describe an app

Five inputs, because these are the only ones the model was able to use. Everything else was dropped.

—

What is moving this prediction

How far the rating shifts if each input alone changes, holding the rest fixed.

Which features the model actually leans on

Permutation importance — how much accuracy is lost when a feature is shuffled. Measured on held-out data, so it reflects real predictive value rather than how often the trees split on it. Bars show the spread across 15 repeats.

How each feature bends the prediction

The model's average response as one feature sweeps its range.

Predicted against actual

Held-out apps the model never saw. A perfect model would put every dot on the diagonal.

Built from the Google Play Store dataset (10,841 apps, 64,295 user reviews). Cleaning, aggregation and model training done in Python with pandas and scikit-learn; the trained gradient boosting model is exported and runs entirely in this page, so nothing you type here leaves your browser.
